key_insight: DED-Agent autonomously builds and calibrates laser directed energy deposition thermal FE models, combining coordinated AI agents with surrogate-assisted parameter search.
engineering_relevance: Automating thermal model setup and calibration can accelerate exploration of additive manufacturing parameters that influence defects, microstructure and properties.
method: A supervisor coordinates intent, simulation and calibration agents through a shared structured specification.
Agents translate plain-language requests into validated specifications, then build, run and check thermal FE models using open-source tools.
Calibration fits heat-source parameters to experimental data using a high-order proper generalized decomposition surrogate within a trust-region search.
evidence_signal: Across five benchmark builds, models ran without manual intervention; simple and medium builds had 4.1–9.1% initial error, reduced to 0.9–2.5% within three calibration rounds, while surrogate errors were 0.08–1.55% and calibration was 5–13× faster.
watch_item: Validation covers five benchmark builds; reliability for broader geometries, materials and process regimes remains to be established.
paper_title: DED-Agent: An agentic AI method for autonomous thermal simulation model development and calibration in laser directed energy deposition
